messages:
incident-bot: Pager: routing.anomaly detected 03:12 UTC. Elevated 5xx rate for requests originating in eu-west -> being routed to us-west fallback. Auto-alert threshold exceeded.

jordan (oncall): seeing it on the dashboard, ~18% of eu traffic hitting us-west, errors up ~12% from baseline. i’m taking first look.

luca: confirmed via telemetry: region_tag mismatches in routing decisions, probes show split decision tree for same client IPs.

maya (netops): dns checks show eu resolver responses sometimes returning the us-west cluster IPs — TTLs still 60s. suspect race in the region-selection cache.

eli (prod-sre): can we rule out BGP/egress? net metrics look fine. this feels like our routing policy evaluation path returned stale policy for a subset of requests.

jordan (oncall): creating incident record: INC-2026354 Sev2 — cross-region routing mismatch affecting eu users. tagging netops + runtime.

incident-bot: Incident INC-2026354 created by jordan (oncall). Pager duty notified.

maya (netops): quick mitigation idea: force failover route for eu traffic to eu-primary via operator CLI, then gradually drain the misrouted backend. suggest reducing DNS TTL to 10s to shorten propagation while we stabilize.

luca: good call. preparing policy rollback patch — looks like a canary policy push at 02:58 caused a race when policy cache updated on some gateways.

jordan (oncall): rolling temporary policy override now. command: ```rbctl routing apply --scope=global --override=eu-only --policy=eu-primary --reason="INC-2026354 mitigation"```

eli (prod-sre): running + verifying. telemetry probe v4 shows steering back to eu-primary for probe set A. errors dropping in that cohort.

support-team: support notes — a handful of customers reported degraded responses (timeouts/500s). CS informed and posting an interim message to affected customers.

maya (netops): TTL lowered to 10s: ```dnsctl zone eu.example.internal set-ttl --record=steer.example 10s``` will take ~TTL window to converge. also flushing edge policy caches where possible.

luca: performing targeted cache invalidation on gateways showing old policy. command: ```gatewayctl invalidate-cache --tag=policy-v202602 --region=eu-west1```

jordan (oncall): handing off to eli for next hour — i'm going offline for patch window. eli, please keep the incident hot and escalate to networking if we see reappearance.

eli (prod-sre): taking handoff. current status: policy override in place, TTL 10s, cache invalidation in progress. observed 5xx rate decreasing from +12% -> +2% in last 6m. continuing to monitor.

incident-bot: INC-2026354 update: status=mitigating, assignee=eli (prod-sre).

maya (netops): root cause hypothesis: race in policy-etcd watchers + async cache write path meant a fraction of gateways evaluated the old policy during a partial rollout. will open a fix PR to add stronger sequencing and a cache-stamp check.

luca: capturing telemetry snapshot for postmortem: ```/opt/tools/trace-grab --incident INC-2026354 --output /tmp/inc-2026354-traces.tgz```

eli (prod-sre): customer impact estimate for now: ~15-25 minutes of elevated errors for ~5% of EU traffic; higher percent only for customers pinned to affected gateways. CS will send an updated advisory.

support-team: copying the advisory to #customers-notify, will include mitigation steps and ETA for RCA.

jordan (oncall): thanks team. i'll add the playbook items and sign off once eli confirms stability. :thumbsup:

eli (prod-sre): stability confirmed for last 10m, no new spikes. I'll keep the incident open for RCA artifacts and bridge notes. transferring to post-incident owner: luca.

incident-bot: INC-2026354 status=monitoring -> root-cause-investigation assigned to luca.

luca: noted. next steps: PR to fix watcher sequencing, add canary gating, and add metric alert for policy-cache divergence. will file the RCA doc and link here.

maya (netops): will also schedule a small runbook change: when TTLs are low during rollouts, add a cache-quiesce step.

eli (prod-sre): handoff complete. last_message_ts=6354010299.
